adventure.title: The Princess on the Salt Road
adventure.synopsis: Before midnight, Kallias’s soldiers wrench the Assembly’s bronze speaking rail from its sockets and hang white command lamps over Aulon. Princess Ianthe—half-elven heir to the old royal house—refuses to name him protector and leaves with the city seal beneath her cloak. Her bodyguards have until the second sunset to carry her thirty-six miles to neutral Myrine, where seven white stones, three magistrates, and the waiting Sea-Lark can place her beyond Kallias’s lawful reach. The open Salt Road buys speed with witnesses. The dry aqueduct hides people but strands horses. Funeral peace binds every blade. Bridge remounts may carry rescue or pursuit, and every reed boat taken from the bank is one a household cannot use. Kallias needs Ianthe alive, the Ash Knives need the last heir dead, and her mother’s kin offer a road so safe that she may reach the coast as their ward rather than Aulon’s free petitioner.
adventure.premise: Princess Ianthe trusts her few household guards to contradict her and still obey. Three nights after King Leandros died, Strategos Kallias occupied the Assembly, gates, mint, and messenger loft, then demanded that Ianthe lend his coup her name. She refused. A neutral league trireme waits at Myrine until the harbor chain rises at the second sunset. Sanctuary begins only when Ianthe crosses seven white stones unbound and speaks before three magistrates in her own voice. Choose which road spends secrecy, which spends time, which households bear the flight, what the bronze seal is permitted to command, and when guarding Ianthe requires releasing control of her.
adventure.explanation:
Aulon balances an old royal house, a citizen Assembly, and a professional strategos elected for war. King Leandros died of fever before physicians, household officers, and Assembly witnesses after the winter campaign; the funeral rolls, sickroom tablets, and public notices agree. Kallias found a divided Assembly, an adult half-elven heir, and an army still answering wartime warrants; he decided that closed gates were safer than an uncontrolled vote. His diagnosis is not wholly false. His remedy is a coup.

Ianthe is twenty-seven, trained in civic law, a practiced rider, and a poor liar. Her mother, Serathiel of the White Cypress, returned to her own people ten years ago after every family appearance became a referendum on foreign rule. Ianthe stayed. She is Aulonite before she is anyone’s elven cousin. The palm-weight bronze seal bears three hills above an open hand. It requisitions horses, opens granaries, and authenticates decrees; it cannot fear, consent, or ask protection. Only Ianthe’s living, uncoerced speech can begin sanctuary. Seal and princess may therefore travel separately.

Kallias sends Captain Dorion Vey under three bounded orders: return Ianthe alive, recover the seal intact, and avoid the public bloodshed that would expose emergency rule as naked tyranny. Kallias wants a protector proclamation that looks voluntary. Dorion never enlarges the warrant in private or pretends it says less than it does. He writes each concession twice, names its witnesses and effective hour, protects Ianthe from assassins because his first order requires a living princess, and resumes the custody demand when the shared danger ends. His exact obedience makes him trustworthy inside a bad warrant and dangerous at its edge.

The Ash Knives have reached the opposite conclusion: neither general nor princess should inherit the crisis. They want Ianthe dead before monarchy can become useful again, and loyalist colors let murder travel inside pursuit. Naevan, Serathiel’s envoy, waits among the Reed Villages with six outriders and a forest road. His protection is real. So is the jurisdiction concealed inside every leaf-sealed promise.

Myrine makes neutrality out of visible labor. Chain crews keep the harbor open. Guards separate armed claimants. A registrar preserves duplicate tablets. Three magistrates ask four plain questions: who are you, whose choice brought you, whom do you fear, and what remedy do you seek? Before the second sunset, the Sea-Lark can carry a lawful petitioner beyond Aulonite reach. Afterward, sanctuary remains, but clean extraction is gone. The road therefore measures time, witnesses, divided custody, public authorship, and the duty to protect a woman who retains the right to decide what her safety is for.

references.title: Princess Ianthe Aulonid
references.summary: Aulon's twenty-seven-year-old half-elven heir, trained in civic law and determined that protection preserve her informed choice, living voice, and public authorship.
references.content:
## Aulonite before anyone's ward

Princess Ianthe Aulonid is the adult heir of Aulon's old royal house, daughter of King Leandros and Serathiel of the White Cypress. She is twenty-seven, trained in civic law, a practiced rider, and a poor liar. When Serathiel returned to her own people, Ianthe stayed. She understands herself as Aulonite before anyone's elven cousin, protected guest, or political instrument.

## Counsel me plainly

Ianthe trusts guards who will contradict her and still obey the decision once she has heard the cost. She asks exact questions, notices who has not spoken, dislikes theatrical courage, and becomes more formal when afraid. Her protection compact treats understanding, voluntary choice, and the ability to speak publicly as things an escort must preserve rather than obstacles to be removed.

## A living voice, not a bronze command

The bronze seal can requisition horses, open granaries, and authenticate decrees. It cannot consent, fear, petition, or speak for Ianthe. Only her living, uncoerced speech can begin Myrine sanctuary, and she may separate her person from the seal or delegate work without surrendering authorship. Her route, condition, custody, promises, petition, decisions, and political acts remain live adventure state.

references.title: Strategos Kallias Arven
references.summary: Aulon's wartime strategos, whose plausible diagnosis of a constitutional crisis became a coup built around military continuity, controlled testimony, and Ianthe's apparent assent.
references.content:
## War office beneath white lamps

Kallias Arven is Aulon's professional strategos, elected for war while King Leandros lived. After the king died before physicians, household officers, and Assembly witnesses, Kallias faced a divided Assembly, an adult half-elven heir, and an army still answering wartime warrants. He chose occupied gates, closed institutions, and command lamps over an uncontrolled vote. His diagnosis is not wholly false. His remedy is a coup.

## Continuity in another person's voice

Kallias wants emergency rule to look like lawful continuity. A living Ianthe, an intact bronze seal, and a protector proclamation that appears voluntary can make military control resemble constitutional consent. Public bloodshed, contradictory witnesses, and records he does not control expose the difference. His political method therefore values disciplined force, bounded warrants, and a public account in which armed retainers appear to be the danger.

## Command cannot manufacture assent

The strategos can issue military warrants, direct officers, hold civic infrastructure, and argue that order requires protection. He cannot make coerced speech free, make the seal consent, or replace Myrine's sanctuary judgment with Aulonite command. His operative orders, force locations, pursuit posture, reports, concessions, custody claims, and changing public account belong to encounters and the pursuit, custody, beacon, and harbor instruments.

references.title: Captain Dorion Vey
references.summary: Kallias's recovery captain, exact inside a bad warrant: he records every bounded concession, protects the principal his commission requires alive, and never mistakes tactical cooperation for consent.
references.content:
## Exact obedience inside a bad warrant

Dorion Vey is the captain Kallias trusts with politically dangerous recovery work because he neither enlarges a clause in private nor pretends it says less than it does. He writes concessions twice, names their witnesses and effective hour, and expects every exception to survive later review. That exactness makes him trustworthy inside a bad warrant and dangerous at its edge.

## A living principal, intact evidence, public restraint

The commission that sends Dorion onto the road is framed around a living Ianthe, an intact bronze seal, and avoidance of public bloodshed that would reveal emergency protection as naked coercion. He can negotiate acts he has authority to defend, protect Ianthe from assassins because a dead principal defeats the commission, and acknowledge limits visible in older law or neutral procedure. He does not promise a city, office, or political settlement he cannot give.

## A truce is not consent

Dorion separates shared defense, physical control, written terms, and political assent. Fighting the same assassin does not settle custody; accepting protection from one attack does not ratify Kallias; and a tactical formation does not become Ianthe's choice. His current pursuit stage, contact, force, operative clauses, concessions, cooperation, truce, custody claim, and location remain live state in the specialist records.

references.title: Naevan of the White Cypress
references.summary: Ianthe's White Cypress cousin and Serathiel's envoy, who offers real protection while naming the jurisdiction carried by every forest road and leaf-sealed promise.
references.content:
## Envoy beneath the white cypress

Naevan is Ianthe's cousin and Serathiel's envoy beyond Aulon. He speaks for a household able to shelter kin, move through forest country, and defend people placed under its protection. He does not arrive as an Aulonite officer, a neutral magistrate, or a bodyguard under the escort's command.

## Name aid and custody separately

Naevan distinguishes temporary assistance from full household reception and refuses to disguise one as the other. A bounded request should name the help, the people protected, the endpoint, and the road back; full reception places the protected person under White Cypress authority until that authority judges the danger ended. The distinction is part of his integrity, not a hidden exception discovered after agreement.

## Protection carries jurisdiction

Naevan will fight assassins and defend people lawfully under his protection. He will not serve under Aulonite command, attack an Aulonite captain merely for pursuing a warrant, or enter Myrine as an armed company entitled to ignore its lanes. His current presence, route, available aid, written terms, separation point, extraction status, and any custody outcome remain live adventure state.

references.title: Serathiel of the White Cypress
references.summary: Ianthe's elven mother, whose distant household can make her daughter genuinely safe while also deciding when kin-protection ends and political wardship begins.
references.content:
## The mother who left Aulon

Serathiel of the White Cypress is Ianthe's mother. She returned to her own people ten years before the road, after every family appearance in Aulon became a referendum on foreign rule. Ianthe stayed. The separation left real kinship, affection, and political suspicion on both sides of any later offer of protection.

## A court behind the forest road

Serathiel's household has standing to receive Ianthe as kin and the power to keep ordinary Aulonite pursuit from simply taking her back. That safety is not neutral sanctuary. White Cypress protection carries its own judgment about danger, departure, and who may act for a protected guest; hospitality, kinship authority, and wardship are distinct possibilities rather than interchangeable words.

## Kinship cannot speak the petition

Serathiel may authorize an envoy and household protection, but neither motherhood nor superior safety turns an imposed transfer into Ianthe's choice or speaks a Myrine petition in her place. Any active offer, accepted limit, communication right, destination, custody arrangement, or political authorship remains live state in the escort ledger and aftermath record.

references.title: The Sable Courier Houses
references.summary: A family courier network whose city dye house, hill station, marks, ledgers, and household obligations carry people and testimony without making royal service free.
references.content:
## Two houses, one road

The Sable family has maintained royal courier houses for three generations. The House of Blue Lamps is a working dye house inside Aulon with old palace access behind its cistern. The House at Three Cypresses is a limestone change station where the city exits converge, separate, and hand riders toward the bridge or reeds. Myrto Sable keeps the city house; her elder sister Thessa keeps the hill station; Thessa's daughter Eleni knows the official riders, bridge mast, and first reed channels.

## Marks that travel

Courier badges, shutter lamps, route tokens, dry-well signs, ledgers, recognition phrases, and named fallbacks let separated people coordinate without sharing one road. None is self-authenticating. Marks age, codes change, badges are copied or stolen, and a message is only as trustworthy as its chain of people and records.

## Service leaves an account

The houses serve the road through finite labor, animals, shelter, local knowledge, and reputation. Their ledgers also preserve royal arrears, requisitions, fines, repairs, and the names of households made to bear official travel. A prince or princess may request service and issue an obligation; rank does not turn the household into expendable scenery or guarantee that a later government will pay.

## A network, not sanctuary

The Sable houses can relay, provision, hide, witness, or divide a journey within their actual capacity. They cannot erase who passed, make a copied token true, guarantee that a station remains safe, or decide custody for the person they assist. Current household presence, available stores and mounts, arrests, damage, signals, messages, route knowledge, and accepted obligations remain live encounter and ledger state.

references.title: The Gate of Horns
references.summary: Aulon’s public southern gate, where the royal-house charter, livestock traffic, witnesses, and the mounted Salt Road make passage fast and reviewable.
references.content:
## A gate built to be seen

The Gate of Horns opens Aulon directly onto the Salt Road. Paired towers, a broad road court, a livestock wicket, and nearby remount facilities make it the city's fastest mounted exit. Traders, drovers, clerks, soldiers, and citizens can all see how passage is requested and refused; secrecy is the one protection the gate does not offer.

## Charter before command

The older gate charter reserves passage for the royal household until the Assembly performs the civic act required to suspend that privilege. Wartime command may inspect travelers, regulate weapons, and execute a bounded order, but it does not silently become the judgment the charter names. A gate officer therefore needs the authority presented, the exact act requested, and a record fit for later inquiry.

## The straight road

Beyond the towers, the pavement continues toward Red Bridge. The Heron mile-stone marks a reedward turn, while courier and ridge spurs can reach the House at Three Cypresses. The direct road preserves horses, speed, and public testimony; those same surfaces make a departing company easier to name and pursue.

The gate's current doors, guards, orders, witnesses, remounts, traffic, passage decision, and any breach of charter remain live encounter state.

references.title: The Cypress Gate
references.summary: Aulon’s western funeral gate and old road, protected between the inner arch and last stone lion by a visible civic peace older than military command.
references.content:
## The road reserved for the dead

The Cypress Gate opens from Aulon's western wall into an older necropolis and the funeral road. It exists so processions do not cross the market. Gate keys, procession books, tomb wardens, family witnesses, and wheel marks preserve a civic memory that does not depend on the strategos of the day.

## The funeral peace

Between the inner arch and the last stone lion, no officer may arrest, no enemy may proclaim a blood feud, and no living hand may draw steel. The peace is civic rather than magical: breaking it remains physically possible and publicly legible. Wardens may bind weapons, test a mourning claim, surround a suspect without blades, and record who broke the peace and why.

## Roads after the lion

The funeral road carries horses south through tombs and abandoned vineyards. A hidden postern reaches the Horn road; a vineyard crossing reaches the Salt Road above Red Bridge; a farther causeway turns toward the reedward channels. The route trades open force for custom, witnesses, restraint, and slower travel.

Current processions, wardens, observers, assassins, weapon bindings, testimony, route choice, and any breach or preservation of the peace remain live encounter state.

references.title: The Red Bridge
references.summary: Six red arches joining the mounted road, remount post, signal mast, crossing register, lower works, and Heron Sluice without making control of one control of all.
references.content:
## One post, several systems

Six red-stone arches carry the Salt Road across Kestros Gorge. The western abutment joins the remount stable, signal mast, bridge counterweights, crossing office, maintenance ledge, and Heron Sluice. The deck's customary red line separates the old Aulon road district from Myrine's protected trade corridor; it is a place for bounded parleys and transfers, not a sanctuary boundary.

## Work that must be named

The older road code, later warrants, requisition receipts, signal entries, water accounts, and crossing register make bridge action reviewable. A defensible order identifies the resource, duration, witnesses, and person who answers afterward. Broad allegiance does not explain who may spend horses, close a barrier, send a political signal, or change village water.

## Separate control surfaces

The deck carries wagons and mounted companies. The stable changes pace. The mast sends claims toward Beacon Hill. The lower ledge bypasses the deck for people and light equipment. The Heron Sluice feeds the upper reed channels. Holding, disabling, or authorizing one surface does not automatically grant the others, and damage to one function creates costs elsewhere.

Current control, personnel, remount numbers, signals, register entries, bridge damage, barrier position, water state, pursuit, truce, requisitions, and civilian consequences remain live encounter and operations-sheet state.

references.title: The Reed Villages
references.summary: Three linked settlements whose boats, pilots, households, channels, and shared water turn concealment and evacuation into finite civic choices.
references.content:
## Three settlements, not one refuge

Kalamai dries mats along the upper channels. Vathys stands on piles around the black basin. Nesos occupies a low island beside the pilots' eastward run and a traveler shrine near harbor water. Together they form a working community of households, pilots, landings, fish boards, drying racks, boats, and obligations rather than a blank place for fugitives to disappear.

## Four named waters

The broad Salt Cut carries large craft, horses, and visible companies. The narrow Black Thread offers concealment to small groups that trust a pilot. Pilots' Run reaches the eastern landing below Beacon Hill quickly enough to be read and followed. The Cypress Drain turns west toward the forest boundary and does not lead to Myrine. The Heron Sluice above the villages changes all four by changing water rather than by changing their names.

## Capacity has owners

A hull used for a principal is unavailable to a witness, wounded traveler, horse, prisoner, child, or household. Pilots possess route knowledge that a map cannot replace, and household craft remain civilian property even when a seal or soldier can compel their use. The villages can support concealment, a public flotilla, route division, evacuation, or testimony only by assigning a visible cost.

Current boats, pilots, sureties, confiscations, water level, fires, households, prisoners, routes, pursuers, aid, testimony, and civilian losses remain live encounter and operations-sheet state.

references.title: Beacon Hill
references.summary: The last height above Myrine, where a visible code, authenticated clay strip, ledger entry, witnesses, and three unequal descents shape the harbor’s first interpretation.
references.content:
## The hill that supplies the first nouns

Beacon Hill stands between the inland road and Myrine Harbor. From its crown, the keeper can see the Red Bridge mast, reed channels, harbor approaches, and the upper works beyond the breakwater. Its low wall cannot decide a battle. Its basket, shutters, speaking trumpet, message route, and visible formations tell the harbor whether to prepare for a traveler, armed company, disputed authority, assassination danger, or petition.

## A signal has a chain

A formal message joins a visible code, the keeper's brass seal on a clay strip, and a ledger entry naming the observer or authority behind it. Seizing the basket changes what the harbor sees; it does not authenticate the hand, timing, witness, or conclusion. The keeper may report what was received, observed, or tested without deciding Ianthe's freedom or Aulon's government.

## Three descents, three destinations

The Salt Steps are the fastest and most public route toward the white stones. The Olive Stairs conceal a foot party through terraces and the fish market. The Ropewalk Track reaches the chainhouse and league quay rather than sanctuary. Horses, weapons, witnesses, wounded people, a principal, and a disputed object may therefore require separate routes and rendezvous.

Current flame, code, clay strips, ledger custody, keepers, witnesses, route control, weapon posture, arrivals, bell state, descent choices, and harbor inferences remain live encounter and operations-sheet state.

references.title: Myrine Harbor
references.summary: A neutral harbor whose sanctuary depends on visible separation, free crossing, spoken remedy, three recorded judgments, and protected transfer rather than possession of a person or seal.
references.content:
## Neutrality made from visible labor

Myrine Harbor joins the upper spear court, seven white stones, petitioner and claimant lanes, sanctuary hall, registrar's tables, chainhouse, League Walk, fish stairs, and league quay. Guards, chain crews, magistrates, substitutes, registrars, witnesses, and sailors perform different parts of neutrality. No one office owns the entire result.

## The sanctuary sequence

A petitioner establishes identity, armed claimants are separated, and the petitioner crosses the seven stones freely. The petitioner then names self, choice, fear, and requested remedy in a living voice. Three magistrates or publicly entered substitutes record whether they heard free speech and grant protection within Myrine law. Only after the third affirmative record does the harbor transfer the petitioner under sanctuary.

## Protection is not constitutional judgment

Myrine may separate companies, set weapon conditions, protect a hearing, preserve duplicate records, hold disputed property, shelter a petitioner, or transfer someone to lawful transport. It need not decide who should govern Aulon. The bronze seal may establish identity or support a property claim; it cannot cross freely, state a fear, or choose a remedy. A ship may carry a sanctuary transfer; it cannot create one.

Current arrivals, lanes, weapons, witnesses, magistrates, substitutions, petition wording, judgments, records, seal custody, chain position, ship availability, transfer, arrests, and final remedy remain live encounter and operations-sheet state.

references.title: The White Cypress
references.summary: Serathiel’s forest household, whose kin-protection can defeat ordinary pursuit while creating a separate jurisdiction over reception, danger, and departure.
references.content:
## Kinship with institutions behind it

The White Cypress is Serathiel's forest household and court, not a poetic name for private maternal affection. It has standing to receive Ianthe as kin, riders and roads outside ordinary Aulonite relay, and enough force and custom to make its protection real. That protection enters a jurisdiction with its own authority over guests, household danger, and departure.

## Aid and reception are different acts

A bounded request can name guides, scouts, messages, a decoy trail, or evacuation for threatened households, together with endpoint, numbers, duration, and withdrawal. Full reception places the protected person under White Cypress authority until that authority judges the danger ended. Hospitality, limited assistance, kin protection, and wardship must therefore be named rather than exchanged as synonyms.

## Boundaries between roads

White Cypress riders do not become an Aulonite command section merely because they share an enemy. Their household authority does not extend through Myrine's armed lanes, complete an Aulonite petition, or turn a safer destination into Ianthe's unspoken consent. The same limits make a clear offer trustworthy: help is what the record says it is.

Current envoys, riders, messages, aid, terms, written requests, routes, presence, reception, custody, withdrawal, communications, and political authorship remain live encounter, ledger, and aftermath state.

references.title: The Ash Knives
references.summary: Small antimonarchist cells that seek to end the royal succession by exploiting loyalist colors, confined ground, procedural openings, and distrust among larger armed parties.
references.content:
## Neither protector nor heir

The Ash Knives reject the choice between Kallias's emergency government and Ianthe's royal claim. They intend to end the succession before either general or heir can use it. Their objective is distinct from Kallias's custody project even when an attack made in loyalist colors strengthens his account or turns pursuers and bodyguards against one another.

## Few people, prepared openings

The Knives cannot defeat companies in open formation. They use poison, copied tokens, false uniforms, damaged tack, confined routes, panic, fire, hidden blades, compromised messengers, attacks on witnesses and records, and threats to infrastructure or transport. They prefer moments when procedure predictably separates a principal from weapons, guards, or trusted witnesses.

## Confusion is part of the weapon

A successful cell makes each larger force misidentify the danger, spend protection on the wrong surface, or convert temporary cooperation into a custody mistake. Exposing an assassin can create real common defense without making Dorion an ally, proving every escort act lawful, or resolving who speaks for Ianthe.

Current cells, identities, access, weapons, poisons, targets, signals, casualties, captures, testimony, surviving plans, and attack outcomes remain live encounter and operations-sheet state.

references.title: The Aulonite Bronze Seal
references.summary: A palm-weight state seal bearing three hills above an open hand: powerful enough to authenticate and requisition, incapable of consent, fear, petition, or political authorship.
references.content:
## Authority cut into bronze

The Aulonite seal is a palm-weight bronze matrix bearing three hills above an open hand. Within the offices and laws that recognize it, an impression can authenticate decrees, requisition horses or stores, open granaries, commission couriers, and support a claim to public property. The act should leave wax, witnesses, receipts, ledgers, or another record through which the authority can later be reviewed.

## The object and the person do different work

The seal can establish that someone possesses a recognized instrument or that a document bears its impression. It cannot prove who freely chose to use it, whether the bearer is Ianthe, whether an escort acts with continuing consent, or which constitutional claim is just. It cannot cross sanctuary stones, name fear, request protection, or substitute for living speech.

## Portable, divisible, contestable

The seal can travel apart from Ianthe, support a decoy, authenticate a bounded obligation, be deposited as disputed property, or become the subject of a separate recovery effort. Those possibilities make custody of the object politically important without making it custody of the princess.

Current possession, concealment, impressions, requisitions, receipts, loss, damage, impoundment, route, legal effect, and final disposition remain live encounter, ledger, and aftermath state.

encounters.title: The House of Blue Lamps
encounters.summary: In a shuttered dye house below the occupied Assembly, Ianthe lays the bronze seal on a stained table, defines the compact of her protection, and asks which cost the road should spend first.
encounters.opening_view: The bronze speaking rail comes apart three streets uphill, each blow carrying through the dye house. Myrto bars the shutters and sets three route tokens on a red-lined courier board. Ianthe places the royal seal between them as the palace beacon changes from gold to Kallias’s white. Four knocks sound at the door, then one—the correct signal, known to too many hands. Soot marks Ianthe’s cheek; her voice does not shake. “Counsel me plainly.”
encounters.content:
## Situation

Myrto has shuttered the blue lamps and cleared one dye table without cleaning it. Indigo stains the grain, vinegar and wet fleece sharpen the smoke, and the covered cistern still hides the old palace maintenance mouth. Three streets uphill, soldiers are prying the bronze speaking rail from the Assembly steps so no citizen can lawfully call the body to order.

Princess **Ianthe Aulonid** arrived ten minutes ago in a servant’s gray cloak, soot across one cheek and the palace seal under her tunic. She chose this emergency house, dismissed retainers whose uniforms would betray it, and sent for the bodyguards because they are the smallest company she trusts to contradict her and still obey the answer. She is frightened, tired, and entirely present.

Ianthe lays the seal on the stained table. Kallias needs both princess and bronze, but they do different work. An impression can move horses, grain, soldiers, and wax. It cannot cross the white stones or speak the petition Myrine must hear from her.
## Ianthe's compact

Ianthe does not ask the bodyguards to swear that she will never be endangered. She knows such an oath would reward anyone who locked her in a cellar. She asks for three promises:

> Counsel me plainly. Obey when I decide. Do not make me safe by making me absent.

She accepts the same obligations: state what she is preserving, hear objections when time permits, and never spend a bodyguard merely to preserve her dignity. The bodyguards may disagree, delay her, conceal information from enemies, or pull her from immediate danger. Give them her reasons before a decision whenever possible. Her judgment governs the compact. When bodyguards overrule it, the record must name the danger, the act, and the moment at which her authority returns; her own decisions still carry consequences.

Ianthe's objectives, in order, are:

1. Reach Myrine alive and speak a free petition before the second sunset.
2. Prevent Kallias from using her voice or seal to counterfeit lawful continuity.
3. Preserve enough visible Aulonite support that sanctuary does not become permanent foreign wardship.
4. Avoid civil bloodshed where a slower, costlier, or more humiliating road can prevent it.

She can surrender the seal, renounce succession, accept elven protection, or return to Aulon. Each remains possible, but only through her stated assent and a record of who heard it.

## What happened in Aulon

King Leandros died three nights ago after a fever witnessed by physicians, priests, and half the winter council. Kallias did not poison him. The coup began because the old constitutional balance had no accepted answer for a half-elven adult heir, a divided Assembly, and an army whose wartime commander still held emergency warrants.

At dusk, Kallias occupied the Assembly, the mint, the gate towers, and the messenger loft. He announced that Ianthe had asked him to preserve order. She went to the Assembly portico and denied it before soldiers closed the square. Captain Dorion Vey was ordered to escort her back to the palace. Ianthe left through a kitchen court while palace servants raised three different alarms.

Kallias circulates two claims: grief has made Ianthe unfit, and armed retainers are carrying her coastward against sound counsel. Shape the second around the actual bodyguards—foreign blades, Aulonite retainers outside civic command, or local dupes serving a foreign plot. A public appearance can break the abduction story and fix her position in the same moment. Concealment buys distance while Kallias names what the unseen miles mean.

## The hard deadline

Myrine Harbor lies thirty-six road miles southeast. The neutral league trireme **Sea-Lark** arrived for Leandros's funeral and will depart when the harbor chain rises at the second sunset. Its captain has authority to carry a lawful petitioner away from Aulonite jurisdiction, but not to remain while Kallias's cavalry turns the harbor into a battlefield.

The sanctuary steps remain after the ship leaves, but the protection becomes weaker. Myrine can shelter Ianthe inside its walls; it cannot prevent Kallias from surrounding the polis, closing its roads, and demanding arbitration while his version of events hardens. Reaching the harbor after the chain rises is survival, not full success.

Treat delays as visible choices rather than hidden penalties. A public speech, rescued villagers, exhausted mounts, a repaired aqueduct, a negotiated truce, or a careful crossing may cost time. Name the lost distance whenever a choice consumes a meaningful part of the road.

## Three ways out

Myrto has gathered enough current information to make all three departures credible.

### The Gate of Horns

The south gate opens directly onto the Salt Road. It is the fastest path for riders and the best place to produce public witnesses. Kallias has a full squad there, but the gate charter reserves passage for the royal household until the Assembly formally suspends the house. That has not happened. Ianthe can invoke the charter, force the guards to violate it before citizens, or create enough confusion for a mounted break.

The cost is pursuit. The gate remounts can put Dorion on the road within an hour, and every witness can describe the escort.

### The Dry Aqueduct

A maintenance channel beneath the old baths passes under the southeast wall. It cannot take horses, a carriage, or anyone unwilling to crawl through lime dust and old water. The lower sluice was sealed after a collapse, but repair workers still know the cistern access.

The aqueduct offers the longest unseen lead and makes it easy to send the bronze seal by another route. It also leaves the escort on foot in the olive hills, and a badly handled sluice can flood the tunnel or announce the escape at the bath court.

### The Cypress Gate

A small western gate opens into the necropolis and the old funeral road. A sacred truce forbids drawn steel between the inner gate and the last grave marker. Kallias has not closed it because violating the truce would turn every old family against him. Mourning carts depart before midnight with grave cloth, oil, and offerings for Leandros's coming funeral.

The route provides witnesses who value custom more than Kallias. It also requires the escort to protect Ianthe among crowds without openly carrying weapons, and the Ash Knives know that everyone will first suspect the strategos if she dies there.

All three roads reach **the House at Three Cypresses**, an old courier station beyond the first hills. The escort can divide, use a decoy, send the seal separately, or arrange more than one exit. Ianthe will accept separation from the seal. She will not accept being sent unconscious or misinformed down a road selected in her name.

## Keeping the route open

The House at Three Cypresses is the prepared rendezvous. Every exit also continues toward Red Bridge or the Reed Villages, and Myrto can name those broad continuations, though she does not know their present patrols, water, or signals.

- From the Gate of Horns, the Salt Road continues toward the Red Bridge; a marked turn near the Heron mile-stone reaches the reedward towpath.
- From the Dry Aqueduct, an eastern shepherd ridge meets the bridge road, while an old feeder channel runs south-west toward the Heron levee and Reed Villages.
- From the Cypress Gate, a vineyard cross-road bends east toward the bridge, and the funeral road continues toward the reedward causeway.

Skipping the courier house saves time and denies Dorion one predictable rendezvous. It also gives up guaranteed resupply, a controlled counsel circle, early discovery of tampered provisions, and the clearest statement of Dorion's and Naevan's terms. Ianthe asks the escort to name which of those benefits they are deliberately sacrificing. She accepts a direct route when the house is watched, the deadline is tight, or division makes convergence more dangerous than useful.

Clues record where route facts can be discovered or corroborated; roads remain governed by distance, terrain, and control. A later witness who confirms what happened at an earlier gate strengthens the public account without opening a physical road backward through the journey.

## The starting cast

**Princess Ianthe** has not slept, grows more formal as fear rises, and keeps asking who bears each proposed cost. She knows the Salt Road and Myrine's law, and she can shoot from horseback well enough to discourage a pursuer. Formation fighting, assassin searches, repairs, piloting, and sustained defense remain the bodyguards' work.

**Myrto Sable** is broad, sixty, blue to the elbows, and incapable of whispering without sounding angry. She has one cart, four ordinary horses, two palace saddles, mourning cloth, lime workers' tokens, and three changes of clothing. She will remain behind and expects arrest.

**Timon Vale**, Ianthe's seventeen-year-old page, knows every palace rumor and almost no roadcraft. Ianthe wants him sent separately to a relative inside Aulon. Timon insists that public loyalty means nothing if everyone useful leaves. Keeping him adds a vulnerable witness; leaving him creates a future hostage; giving him a decoy task can turn him into an active ally.

## Immediate pressure

Before the route is chosen, someone knocks four times, pauses, and knocks once. That is a correct palace signal used by half a dozen people. The caller is a frightened stable groom with news that Dorion has searched two other safe houses and has not yet reached this street. The groom may be genuine, followed, or an Ash Knife using the signal. In every case, the coup, Dorion's search, and the assassination threat remain in force; the immediate choice is how much the escort reveals while verifying a person under time pressure.

If the house is compromised, Myrto can open the cistern wall, start a dye fire as cover, or drive the cart into the street while the escort uses another exit. Failure changes the departure conditions; it does not end the journey.

reference_links.context: Ianthe defines what protection must preserve: informed choice, a living voice, and authority distinct from the bronze seal.
Kallias's coup, legitimacy strategy, and need for apparent assent define the danger behind every departure.
Dorion is the recovery captain whose exact warrant practice determines what pursuit may demand or concede if it catches the road.
Serathiel's kinship authority explains why the White Cypress alternative can offer genuine safety without becoming neutral sanctuary.
The Sable network explains how the dye house, courier marks, family labor, and the hill rendezvous connect without making any route or resource guaranteed.
The Horns charter and visible mounted road define the fastest public exit without establishing whether the gate is open or who controls passage.
The funeral peace makes the western exit a route of restraint and old-family witness rather than a promise that the procession is safe.
The bridge is the mounted road hinge where speed, public authority, signals, remounts, and water later become separate decisions.
The three villages offer channels and households rather than an unlimited hidden refuge, so every reedward plan must name what its boats are asked to carry.
Myrine sanctuary depends on Ianthe crossing and speaking freely; the harbor, seal, escort, and waiting ship cannot perform that act for her.
The Ash Knives are a separate antimonarchist threat whose use of loyalist colors and procedural openings can make pursuit conceal murder.
The bronze seal can authenticate and requisition but cannot consent, petition, or turn its bearer into Ianthe.

encounters.title: The Gate of Horns
encounters.summary: At Aulon’s south gate, a royal passage charter, a narrowing wicket, and Kallias’s white receipts turn speed into public testimony—or public violence.
encounters.opening_view: Wheels lock against wheels beneath the bronze horns. Kallias’s clerk reads the new warrant—armed retainers detained, Ianthe returned, the royal seal preserved—while the older gate charter remains cut into the tower above him. Soldiers count spearheads; teamsters count soldiers. At the livestock wicket, inspection passes from cargo to faces. Lieutenant Phaedra Corin raises one hand. The wicket narrows around the next traveler before anyone has established whose law governs passage.
encounters.content:
## Situation

Kallias’s white command lamps burn above the paired towers. The great doors are shut, but the livestock wicket remains open because a polis cannot stop eating merely because its constitution has failed. Teamsters count spearheads; citizens linger where they can hear; a clerk reads the new warrant until the words begin to sound older than the paper.

Lieutenant **Phaedra Corin** commands twenty soldiers trained under Leandros and paid by Kallias at dusk. Her order is narrower than the barred gate: detain armed retainers outside civic command, return Ianthe to protected residence, preserve the seal. It neither authorizes killing the princess nor repeals the household passage charter. Phaedra knows both limits—and knows she must survive every decision she postpones until Dorion arrives.
## Ways through

**Invoke the gate charter.** Ianthe may show herself, name the old law, and require Phaedra either to open the road or publicly place Kallias's warrant above the house and Assembly. This creates excellent witnesses and may bring soldiers or citizens into Ianthe's service. It also tells Dorion exactly when and how she left.

**Pass as road traffic.** Mourning cloth, a dye cart, workers' cords, or a convincing inspection dispute can move a small group through the livestock lane. The bronze seal is difficult to conceal from a serious search but can be carried by someone who does not resemble the princess's company.

**Create two truths at once.** Ianthe can appear at the gate while riders, a cart, or the seal depart elsewhere. Kallias's officers are prepared for disguise but not for a princess who publicly declares one intention and then takes another lawful route.

**Break the gate.** The escort can seize the winch, raise the livestock bar, fight through the wicket, or open the doors to the crowd. This is fast once begun and leaves no ambiguity. It also gives Kallias the civil violence he needs for his story.

## Beyond the gate

Three roads show before the escort is fully exposed. A courier spur reaches the House at Three Cypresses. The pavement runs on to Red Bridge and its remounts. At the Heron mile-stone, fish carts take a packed towpath toward the Reed Villages without crossing the bridge deck. Horses lose speed there, and an opened sluice turns earth to mud, but a public departure can still break into concealment before Dorion closes.

Ianthe does not insist on displaying herself merely because this is the public route. She favors an open charter challenge when Kallias's abduction story is the least recoverable threat and the escort has a credible plan for crowd and assassin control. If the escort has already passed covertly, she will not step back into view for symbolism alone. She may instead send a named witness, written declaration, or recognizable supporter to preserve part of the public account.

The escort may bypass the courier house and continue directly toward either middle road. Doing so preserves momentum but forfeits prepared remounts, treatment, and the controlled exchange of offers.

## Protection problem

The danger is not a single line of guards. It is the overlap of soldiers who will not willingly kill Ianthe, hidden Ash Knives who will, and citizens who may surge toward her when they recognize her. A bodyguard can protect her by controlling distance, sight lines, and who reaches her first. Killing every uniformed opponent may make the actual assassin's work easier.

An Ash Knife named **Sera Noll** waits in a grain cart with a short bow under sacks. She will not attack unless Ianthe becomes visible and the crowd gives her a plausible escape. Sera has no special immunity to detection. Her presence should be signaled by a cart entered twice on the tally, a driver who does not know the miller's name, and a clean bowstring in flour dust.

## Consequences

A public passage gives Ianthe named witnesses, possible volunteers, and a direct answer to the abduction story. It also advances Dorion's pursuit and closes easy use of the Red Bridge unless the escort secures remounts or delays the gate cavalry.

A covert passage preserves distance but lets Kallias claim that private blades smuggled the grieving princess away. A violent passage may split the gate soldiers: some pursue, some refuse, and some join. Record who crossed the threshold beside Ianthe. At Myrine, witnesses are not decoration; they can attest that she traveled by choice.

reference_links.context: Ianthe can invoke the household charter and create public testimony only if the escort preserves her ability to choose and speak.
Kallias's command claim depends on making military detention look like protection while older civic law remains visible above the gate.
Dorion's bounded recovery method clarifies what the gate order can require and what an officer cannot silently add while waiting for him.
The gate joins public witness, the royal-house charter, livestock inspection, and the straight mounted road while leaving the actual passage decision live.
The Salt Road continues to the bridge post, where the visible departure can become remount, signal, crossing, and pursuit evidence.
A small Ash Knife cell can exploit inspection, crowding, false loyalist signs, and competing orders without being part of Kallias’s gate command.
The seal may support household passage or travel with a separate bearer, but its presence does not prove Ianthe’s location or assent.

encounters.title: The Dry Aqueduct
encounters.summary: Beneath the baths, lime throats, old water, and a single order of march divide people from horses and force authority to travel as weight.
encounters.opening_view: Once Myrto’s false cistern stone closes, the passage permits only one order of march. Shields turn, packs scrape, and the bronze seal pulls one cloak out of line. Fresh wax shines in a worker’s niche beside a severed maintenance cord. Farther down, a lamp crosses the broken settling bowl and disappears. Overhead, city voices pass without slowing. Ahead, the measured drip becomes a run as pressure gathers behind the swollen lower sluice.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The old southeast aqueduct once carried spring water beneath Aulon’s wall and into the public baths. A raised channel replaced it; an earthquake opened the lower course; magistrates sealed the maintenance mouth rather than pay masons to make the hidden damage honest. Lime workers, smugglers, and children have used pieces of it ever since. The wall remembers traffic the city no longer records.

The route begins behind Myrto’s cistern or beneath the bath furnace and ends in an olive cutting two miles outside the wall. No horse passes. Rigid armor catches at the lime throat; packs travel ahead or behind. A bodyguard who turns to fight may block everyone she protects. Before entry, decide what weight survives the crawl, what authority takes another road, and whether Ianthe or the seal should draw the first search.
## The channel

The aqueduct has three practical sections.

**The lime throat** is narrow enough that travelers move one at a time. Loose stone above it makes noise travel farther than people. A rear guard cannot see the front. Establish marching order and signals before entering; this is bodyguard work, not bookkeeping.

**The broken bowl** is a circular settling chamber with a collapsed roof. Moonlight reaches it through fig roots. **Pela the Limeburner** and two cousins use the chamber to store untaxed lamp oil. Pela will guide the escort, demand payment, ask Ianthe to pardon an imprisoned brother, or sell the route later depending on how she is treated. She is not secretly loyal to either side.

**The lower sluice** is closed by a swollen wooden gate. Opening it clears the exit but releases old water from a side reservoir. The escort can raise it slowly, break it, divert the water through a maintenance crack, or climb the collapse above. A careful repair costs time. A violent opening sends muddy water into the bath drains and tells Aulon where the fugitives went.

## Threats in confined ground

Dorion's soldiers will not enter blindly in force. If they discover the route, they occupy both mouths, send two shielded scouts, and offer terms through the stone. Their aim is to make the bodyguards choose between surrender and exposing Ianthe to a dangerous climb.

The Ash Knives can exploit the same geometry with fewer people. One attacker in front and one behind can turn an escort into separated pairs. Give attentive characters signs: fresh wax on a wall niche, a maintenance cord cut at shoulder height, or a voice repeating a password with the wrong bath-house accent.

Ianthe accepts being placed in the middle of the order. She objects if every competent fighter goes ahead and leaves her with whoever happens to be weakest. She can help hold a lamp, remember old water marks, and speak to Pela without requiring a bodyguard to impersonate her judgment.

## Exiting the channel

The olive cutting provides concealment but no mounts. The Gate of Horns road lies east; the Cypress road lies west; the House at Three Cypresses is six miles south over low ridges. The escort can steal or buy farm animals, continue on foot, rendezvous with a decoy group, or send a fast runner ahead.

The aqueduct's principal reward is an uncertain lead. Dorion may not know which exit was used. Its principal cost is physical: reduced equipment, fatigue, separation, and delayed access to the mounted road. Do not convert those costs into a single test. Let the confined order make them decide what protection means without a clean shield wall.

## Choosing beyond the olive cutting

Water marks, shepherd cairns, and Pela’s knowledge reveal three continuations. The south ridge reaches the House at Three Cypresses. An eastern sheep track drops to the Salt Road north of Red Bridge. The cracked feeder channel runs southwest to the Heron levee above the Reed Villages. It cannot take carts and punishes armor, but it preserves the aqueduct’s ambiguity instead of returning the fugitives to the first obvious road.

Ianthe favors the bridge when the escort can recover mounted speed without giving Dorion immediate control of the remounts. She favors the reeds when pursuit remains unfixed, the principal and seal must stay divided, or the escort has already sacrificed too much equipment to contest a military post. She does not choose the slowest road merely because it is hidden; the second-sunset deadline remains one of the facts she weighs.

An escort that bypasses the courier house receives no automatic meal, fresh tack, or warning about the station's sabotaged cordial. It may reach the middle road earlier and with less complete information.

## If the route closes

A blocked mouth should create a custody problem, not a dead end. Pela knows a vertical furnace shaft that returns to the bath quarter, while the broken bowl opens onto a fig-root climb outside the wall. Either fallback separates the escort from cached equipment and may place Ianthe in public without warning. Dorion can also offer to withdraw from one mouth if the bodyguards surrender the seal or one named escort. He keeps literal terms and exploits anything left unstated.

Ianthe will consider caching the seal, sending it with Pela, or using it to bargain for a clear exit. She asks who will be endangered by each choice and whether the escort can later prove that any transfer was voluntary. The aqueduct should leave the group with a changed arrangement of people and objects, not merely fewer resources.

reference_links.context: Ianthe may separate from the seal or accept hard physical risk, but the escort cannot convert confined movement into authority over her decision.
Kallias controls the city above and the public meaning of an unseen departure, even when his soldiers do not control the old channel.
Dorion's disciplined pursuit remains the relevant recovery standard beyond the aqueduct even though a link does not place him in the tunnel.
Confined order, copied access signs, and separated pairs give a few Ash Knives leverage that they would not have in open formation.
The seal can be cached, bargained, or carried by another route, making object custody distinct from the person moving through the channel.

encounters.title: The Cypress Gate
encounters.summary: The funeral road leaves Aulon under a peace older than Kallias’s warrant: no arrest, no named feud, and no blade drawn before the last stone lion.
encounters.opening_view: Oil lamps and grave cloth are already passing beneath the Cypress Gate. Every soldier’s sword is tied shut; Kallias’s observers wait beyond the last stone lion, where the funeral truce ends. Old Chares counts names against Leandros’s tablet. One hired mourner gives the response for the dead in the wrong order. Another steadies an oil jar with hands too clean for the work. Demea of the Keys lifts the gate key. “Name the peace you ask us to spend.”
encounters.content:
## Situation

Mourning lamps move toward Aulon’s western wall while Kallias’s watchers count carts at both ends of the necropolis. Between the inner arch and the last stone lion, no officer may arrest, no enemy may name a blood feud, and no living hand may draw steel. The peace is civic, visible, and still unbroken; Kallias has not yet taught the city what violating it will cost.

Mourning carts already carry grave cloth, oil, and empty offering jars for Leandros’s funeral. Ianthe can travel veiled among household women, ride openly beside her father’s honor cart, or ask the tomb wardens to name her as a mourner under their protection. Each choice makes a different witness. Each also gives an assassin a crowd in which the bodyguards’ fastest answer is forbidden.
## The wardens

**Old Chares Pell** and **Demea of the Keys** keep the gate. Chares served Leandros and wants Ianthe safely gone. Demea believes using a funeral truce for political escape may destroy the custom for everyone who needs it later. Neither accepts a forged claim of mourning. They can be persuaded by truth, obligation, or a concrete plan to preserve the truce.

A public appeal to the wardens produces witnesses from old Aulonite families. It also obliges Ianthe to answer whether she intends to return with foreign soldiers. Her answer is: she intends to return with a free Assembly if Aulon will still have one. She will not promise that no war can follow.

## Protection without drawn steel

The bodyguards may carry bound weapons, walking staves, shields used as bier boards, or tools. Drawing a blade does not summon divine punishment. It breaks a civic peace that everyone present can see. An attacker who forces that choice may win politically even if killed.

The Ash Knives place two members among hired mourners. Their preferred method is not a dramatic charge. One overturns an oil jar and starts a panic; the other reaches Ianthe with a grave needle treated in ordinary poison. Clues include funeral phrases spoken in the wrong order, hands without oil stains, and a mourner who watches the escort instead of the cart.

Kallias's observers will not assist an assassination unless they mistake the bodyguards for the threat. Captain Dorion, if present, will help stop a visible killer and then demand that Ianthe accept his protection. This can produce a tense temporary alignment without making Dorion an ally.

## The old road

Beyond the stone lion, the funeral road bends south through family tombs and abandoned vineyards. Horses can travel it, though carts move slowly. A hidden postern connects east toward the Gate of Horns road. The House at Three Cypresses lies seven miles ahead.

The route's reward is civic legitimacy among old families and a passage Kallias hesitates to profane. Its cost is restraint. Bodyguards who preserve Ianthe by respecting the truce gain witnesses and perhaps tomb-warden guides. Those who save her by turning the necropolis into a battlefield still save her, but Kallias can say the old peace ended under her colors.

## Roads beyond the last lion

The courier house lies seven miles down the funeral road, but the procession need not reach it. Beside the tomb of the Broken Oar, a vineyard cross-road runs east to the Salt Road above Red Bridge. Farther south, the funeral road meets a causeway once used to carry the drowned from flooded farms; guides can enter the Salt Cut there. Warden keys, procession books, and wheel marks disclose both turns.

The old-family witnesses need not remain physically beside Ianthe to matter. A named mourner may continue openly toward the bridge while Ianthe turns into the reeds, or carry a written account back into Aulon while the escort uses a quieter road. Such division protects only what the witness actually saw. It does not let another person complete Ianthe's petition.

Ianthe favors this exit when custom and testimony can prevent broader military violence. She will not deliberately expose a funeral procession merely to acquire sympathetic witnesses. If assassins have fixed the procession or the wardens cannot protect the crowd, she supports leaving the carts, taking a cross-road, or surrendering the political advantage of the truce.

## Words beneath the truce

The funeral peace also limits accusation. A person may name a danger but may not proclaim a blood feud or demand immediate vengeance. Ianthe can state that Kallias has exceeded his warrant, ask the old families to witness her departure, and promise a free convocation. She cannot lawfully call them to arms until the procession passes the last lion. This gives the bodyguards time to read the crowd and forces every faction to speak more carefully than it fights.

If the escort exposes an Ash Knife without drawing steel, the wardens can surround the suspect with bier poles and grave cloth. If the escort breaks the truce first, Chares still opens the road to save Ianthe, but Demea records exactly who drew and why. That record can preserve the truth of an unavoidable act while denying the escort the political benefit of restraint.

reference_links.context: Ianthe's public authorship and willingness to accept restraint make the funeral peace a political route rather than mere concealment.
Kallias hesitates to profane a peace whose violation would expose the limits of his emergency legitimacy before old families.
Dorion can oppose an assassin under the truce without treating the temporary alignment as Ianthe's assent to recovery.
The necropolis peace constrains arrest, feud, and drawn steel through a visible civic record rather than an invisible prohibition.
The Ash Knives use crowds, ritual knowledge, panic, and hidden weapons because the funeral peace limits the bodyguards’ fastest response.

encounters.title: The House at Three Cypresses
encounters.summary: A courier house offers four horses, finite stores, suspect provisions, and rival terms; every preparation gives Dorion another mile.
encounters.opening_view: Four saddled horses stand in a courtyard expecting more riders than they can carry. Thessa Sable has divided the remaining food into named bundles; Eleni records every arrival and departure while a lookout calls the northern ridge. One girth has been restitched. A white-cloth message offers transfer to Dorion, and a leaf-sealed letter offers a road that never reaches Myrine. The stable doors are closing. Every additional preparation costs distance from the pursuit.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The House at Three Cypresses stands where three roads become one long enough for an ambush and separate again before the coast. The courier house is low limestone, half sunk into the hill, with a springhouse older than its kitchen and a stable cut into the slope. Three black trees show above every ridge. Royal riders once changed horses here without touching the ground. Tonight the pennant hook carries a strip of surrender cloth tied by someone who expects the next traveler to halt before asking whose surrender it is.

**Thessa Sable**, Myrto’s elder sister, keeps the station with a courier’s inventory and a householder’s memory. She has four fresh horses, two tired mares, one mule, road clothes for six, three badges, a covered dispatch cart, barley, water, and names for every family punished after a royal messenger slept beneath her roof. She has no room for a siege and no influence capable of erasing a witness.

Here the escort chooses its shape: rested or moving, disguised or witnessed, united or divided. Every remount, inspection, decoy, evacuation, and negotiation attaches to a person, object, or hour. The house can improve almost any plan, never all of them, before Dorion’s information becomes a road beneath his horses.
## Arrival by route

Carry the consequences of the chosen exit into the first view of the house.

### From the Gate of Horns

The escort arrives mounted, comparatively fresh, and already named. Citizens and gate soldiers saw Ianthe choose the road. That testimony weakens Kallias's abduction story, but Dorion knows which ridge to ride. Unless the escort created a decoy or delayed the gate report, begin with the pursuit **Named** and close enough that a herald can reach the house during the first substantial preparation.

Thessa has heard the public horn sequence. She opens the stable immediately and asks which witnesses can be trusted to repeat what they saw. Her concern is not whether Ianthe is legitimate. It is whether the road can carry the truth faster than cavalry.

### From the Dry Aqueduct

The escort arrives on foot, dirty with lime, and materially worn. Dorion may still be **Unfixed**, but the escort needs the house more: the fresh horses, dry clothing, food, and chance to tend injuries are difficult to refuse. Mud, wet footprints, a broken maintenance grate, or a captured helper can still name the route.

Thessa does not congratulate them on cleverness. She sends Eleni to close the springhouse drain and asks whether anyone followed the watercourse. The concealment bought a lead, not immunity.

### From the Cypress Gate

The escort arrives slower, accompanied by funeral witnesses or at least protected by their memory. Weapons may still be peace-bound. Dorion probably knows the route, but he must decide whether closing openly on mourners and grave wardens is worth the political cost. Begin the pursuit **Named** but not automatically **Closing**.

Thessa receives the mourners at the front door rather than hiding them in the stable. Ianthe can ask them to carry testimony back toward Aulon, continue toward Myrine, or leave before the station becomes a target. Each choice changes who bears the next consequence.

### Split arrivals

The house can reunite separated bodyguards, Ianthe, and the bronze seal. Do not assume all parts arrive together. A seal-bearing decoy may reach first and discover that the station has been watched. Ianthe may arrive without the fastest rider. The absent part remains an active objective rather than being silently restored between encounters.

## If the rendezvous is skipped or missed

The house serves the road; it does not own it. At a dry well half a mile north, one cypress twig points toward Red Bridge, two crossed reeds toward the Heron levee, and an empty niche warns that the station is watched. A group may continue without entering. Later arrivals find a wax tablet with road, travel window, recognition phrase, and fallback only if the first group spent time leaving one.

Do not force separated groups to wait until everyone converges. The group with Ianthe decides whether the benefits of reunion outweigh a worsening pursuit posture. The seal group, witnesses, or decoy may continue independently under the route-split procedure. If the house has burned or fallen to Dorion, the springhouse drain still reaches the western orchard, and the dry-well marks can direct survivors toward either middle road.

Skipping or missing the house has exact costs: no guaranteed remount allocation, no full household meal or treatment, no controlled discovery of the tampered cordial and tack, and incomplete knowledge of one or both custody offers. It also saves a meaningful part of the road and denies the pursuit a fixed convergence point.

## The household and its claim

Thessa does not greet Ianthe with inherited loyalty. She puts two names on the stable table: **Petran Vos** and **Alea Nym**, arrested yesterday for repairing mounts used by Assembly messengers. Their families have been fined. Before the house spends another horse or hides another rider, Thessa wants them released, the fines canceled, and any damage done here entered in the royal accounts under Ianthe's own seal.

Her daughter **Eleni Sable** is twenty-two, a strong rider, and angry enough to volunteer for any decoy plan before understanding its limits. Eleni knows the Red Bridge signal mast, the first three reed channels, and the faces of most official couriers. She does not know how to survive a cavalry search merely because she rides well. Thessa will let her choose, but not let the bodyguards call an uninformed sacrifice a volunteer.

Ianthe knows both women. Leandros once used the house as a hunting lodge and left the courier staff to sleep in the stable. At seventeen, Ianthe found the arrangement funny. At twenty-seven, she remembers it with shame. She does not ask Thessa for loyalty as though it were free. She can use the bronze seal to issue a compensation warrant, name Petran and Alea as royal couriers, or promise later redress in her own hand. The seal can make the promise legible; it cannot ensure that Ianthe ever regains power to honor it.

This relationship sharpens the escort's central duty. Protecting Ianthe does not make every helper expendable, but neither does Ianthe have the right to spend her bodyguards indefinitely repairing the monarchy's old debts. Thessa asks for a decision, not a confession.

## What the house can provide

The following resources are concrete: expose them to inspection, allocation, alteration, or refusal.

- **Four fresh horses.** All are sound after inspection. One is a broad gray mare suited to an armored rider; one is a fast bay that will not tolerate an unfamiliar cloak flapping behind the saddle.
- **Two tired courier mares.** They can reach the Red Bridge at a controlled pace or carry light riders toward the reeds. Hard riding risks lameness.
- **One pack mule and a covered dispatch cart.** The cart is too slow for the direct road but useful as a visible decoy, casualty wagon, or means of moving a household.
- **Road clothing for six.** Salt merchants, shrine servants, and courier gray are available. The clothes change recognition at distance, not Ianthe's face before anyone who knows her.
- **Three courier badges.** One is current, one belongs to a dead rider whose face is known at the Red Bridge, and one was reported stolen before the coup. The stolen badge can pass a hurried villager and provoke immediate detention at a military post.
- **The signal box.** Shutter plates and lamp glass can send the old royal sequences for safe station, pursuit, false message, and wounded courier. Kallias has changed some official codes; Thessa knows which ones only through yesterday.
- **The hidden loft.** Five people can lie behind the grain wall. Searchers who know courier-house construction will find it given time. It is a pause, not sanctuary.
- **Food, water, and basic treatment.** A short halt restores judgment and catches developing poison or strain. A full sleep spends most of the lead gained in Aulon.

## The tampered remount

The Ash Knives came first under a stolen loyalist token. They cut nearly through the bay’s restitched girth and dosed the sun-marked cordial with enough hellebore to leave Ianthe confused, weak, and visibly dependent within an hour. They do not need a clean death here. A fall, a medical panic, or a custody struggle over a princess who cannot speak creates the opening they want.

The tampering is discoverable without a special ability. The girth has fresh wax where old leather should be dry; the stitching turns the opposite direction from Thessa's work; the cordial smells medicinal beneath the honey. Eleni remembers that the false courier touched both items. A careful tack inspection, tasting protocol, questioning the household, or simply choosing different equipment defeats the attempt.

If the escort misses it, fail forward. The bay's girth parts under stress rather than at a predetermined lethal moment. The cordial sickens Ianthe rather than killing her outright. The escort must then protect an injured or impaired principal, prove the condition was engineered, and decide whether bodily incapacity permits temporary decisions on her behalf. Dorion will help prevent her death and use her incapacity to argue for custody. The Ash Knives may attack during that dispute.

## Ianthe's counsel circle

Before the escort chooses the coast road, Ianthe closes the stable doors, puts the seal where everyone can see it, and requires each person to name four things: the road they recommend, the cost they expect someone else to bear, the point at which they would reverse, and the person authorized to make that reversal. She listens first to whoever has spoken least.

Ianthe does not reward theatrical certainty. When someone calls the bridge defensible, she asks who loses water if it is damaged. When someone proposes division, she asks what true thing the decoy carries and how its riders return. When someone asks for public witness, she asks where the witness stands during the first arrow. When someone asks for rest, she asks what bodily sign will end it.

Her own habit is to separate possession, law, and authorship: “Who can move me? Whose rule claims the right? Who will be believed when I say why I went?” Under fear she becomes more formal, not less. The bodyguards may dispute every answer. Once she decides, she states the order, the reason, and the condition that would make her reconsider.
## Dorion's white-cloth offer

Dorion sends no demand shouted from horseback. A herald approaches beneath white cloth with a tablet listing names, releases, hours, and limits. Dorion offers amnesty for Ianthe’s household escort, release of specified road detainees, medical care, and a public return under escort if Ianthe signs a protector proclamation lasting thirty days. The bronze seal will be deposited in the temple treasury and opened only for orders countersigned by Kallias and two named councilors.

At **Contact**, the herald remains outside the wall while Dorion places riders where the house can see that refusal has a road cost. The herald carries two copies of every term. Dorion initials changes on both tablets, gives one to the house, and states the effective hour before witnesses. He speaks in bounded verbs: *release these people; hold this object; delay until this date; permit these witnesses*. He does not say Kallias is harmless. He says exactly what his warrant allows and asks the escort to compare those terms with the blood, hunger, and uncertainty of the remaining road.

His weakness is the same precision. He cannot promise a free Assembly, withdraw Kallias’s soldiers from the civic buildings, or make a proclamation voluntary after Ianthe enters private custody. When pressed, he says, “I can give you thirty days with names attached. I cannot give you the city you wish had survived dusk.”
### What Dorion may negotiate

Dorion can alter the place and visibility of transfer, permit named witnesses, let the bodyguards retain weapons longer, exchange written copies of the orders, release wounded or low-level detainees within his authority, and agree to a limited conference at the Red Bridge. He can grant a temporary truce to identify assassins, recover casualties, clear civilians, or cross dangerous ground. He can promise that neither side will use the truce to improve a firing position, though both may continue sending messages.

He can also accept a narrower temporary arrangement: Ianthe rides under joint observation to the Red Bridge, where she hears Kallias's terms through envoys while remaining physically beside her bodyguards. Dorion will regard any movement past the bridge toward Myrine as a breach.

### What Dorion cannot concede

Dorion will not permit Ianthe to continue to Myrine, enter elven custody, retain the bronze seal after surrender, command Aulonite outposts against Kallias, or make restoration of the Assembly a precondition. He cannot guarantee that Kallias will stop pressing Ianthe after thirty days. He will not say otherwise when asked directly.

He also will not knowingly stand aside for an assassination. Evidence of Ash Knife activity can produce immediate cooperation. When the threat is contained, he resumes the demand for custody unless the situation has materially changed.

### Ways to answer

The escort may reject the offer, publish it, negotiate for time, propose witnesses, feign acceptance, attempt to turn Dorion against Kallias, or attack. Feigned acceptance can buy a short interval, but Dorion requires visible steps: the seal placed on the table, the carriage admitted, or Ianthe moving toward his line. A bare promise does not freeze him.

Killing the herald or striking under white cloth destroys a useful channel, hardens the public abduction story, and makes Dorion rely on containment rather than parley. Capturing the herald can yield messages; it also tells every road post that the escort treats formal exchange as combat.

## Naevan's leaf-sealed offer

Naevan does not arrive with a banner. A white-cypress leaf, still green at the cut, is pinned to the orchard door, and his voice comes from beyond the wall before his outriders show themselves. He offers a forest road, fresh mounts, healers, and six bows no Aulonite relay can count. Full acceptance places Ianthe beneath Serathiel’s household protection until White Cypress judges the danger ended.

Naevan’s language is hospitable enough to hide a border. He speaks of receiving, sheltering, carrying home, and letting the roads close behind her. He does not threaten Ianthe. He believes kinship creates duties that precede the polis’s failure and that a daughter returned alive may argue about jurisdiction later.

When Ianthe asks the term of wardship, the authority that can end it, and whether Aulonite witnesses may accompany her, Naevan answers honestly and incompletely. “Your mother’s door has never been barred to you.” Ianthe replies, “A door is not an answer. Who holds the key after I cross it?” Limited aid is possible only when destination, duration, numbers, and withdrawal are written before his scouts join the road.
### Limited elven aid

Naevan has authority to offer less than full extraction, but not without a record. If Ianthe writes that she requested aid from her mother's kin, he may:

- lend two outriders as scouts as far as Beacon Hill;
- send one guide and false trail with a seal-bearing decoy;
- carry messages through the reed channels; or
- evacuate two threatened households across the forest boundary.

The written request makes the aid lawful within elven custom and makes Kallias's foreign-influence argument easier to prove. Naevan will not place his people under Aulonite military command, attack Dorion solely for executing a recovery warrant, or enter Myrine Harbor as an armed elven company. He may fight the Ash Knives or defend a threatened household regardless of politics.

Ianthe takes the offer seriously. If the escort is broken, she is poisoned, the Ash Knives have fixed her position, or Myrine has become unreachable, the forest road may preserve the only person who can later contest Kallias. She also understands that accepting it abandons immediate supporters to Kallias's story and may make every later return look like foreign intervention.

## Preparations and meaningful delay

Do not turn the station into an arbitrary menu with two action points. Ask what the escort actually does and tell them when a plan requires a meaningful portion of the road. The following normally consume enough time for the pursuit posture to worsen or for another arrival to occur:

- giving the whole escort a full meal, treatment, and sleep;
- refitting every rider and redistributing armor and packs;
- preparing a convincing cart or mounted decoy;
- sending and waiting for a reply from the Red Bridge or Reed Villages;
- evacuating Thessa's household and records;
- conducting extended negotiations with Dorion or Naevan; or
- searching the surrounding ridges thoroughly for watchers.

Brief counsel, a careful tack inspection, changing a few garments, filling water, reading messages, and issuing one clear order do not each consume a separate interval. Reward coherent delegation. A divided escort can prepare several things at once while accepting reduced protection around Ianthe.

State what the delay means in the fiction: dust on the western ridge, a courier lamp changing, horses heard below the spring, or the shadow of the cypresses shortening toward noon. The pressure should be legible enough that they can choose it.

## Choosing the second half of the road

### Red Bridge

The direct road preserves mounted speed and reaches the only remount post capable of refreshing the whole escort. It also runs through military infrastructure. The bronze seal can command the bridge, but using it leaves an authenticated trail. Dorion can concentrate there if the pursuit is Named or Closing.

Choose Red Bridge when speed, command authority, a public confrontation, or control of the pursuit's horses matters more than concealment.

### Reed Villages
